guides.title: Circle rate and guidance value: what the official texts say
guides.description: What circle rate, guidance value, fair value, collector rate and ready reckoner mean in the states Payotte could read, and how they change the stamp duty base.
guides.answer: A circle rate (the term varies by state: guidance value, fair value, collector rate, ready reckoner, guideline land rate) is the minimum value per area or plot that the state uses to charge stamp duty and registration fee. Where the sheets Payotte read say so, the charge is on the higher of the price in your deed and the reference value. The name, the way it is fixed and the lookup page differ in every state; there is no central list. This guide gives only what the official texts read say.

guides.title: Stamp duty and registration charges in India, by state
guides.description: How stamp duty and registration fees work when you buy a home in India, the states whose rates Payotte could read, and where to check the rest.
guides.answer: Buying a home in India triggers two separate charges, stamp duty and a registration fee, and both are set by the state or union territory, not by the Centre. Each is a percentage of the price or of the state's reference value, usually whichever is higher. Payotte could read the official rate for only seven jurisdictions (Maharashtra, Kerala, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, Odisha, Chandigarh and Puducherry); stamp duty on a sale runs from 4% to 10% among them. For every other state, check the state's own registration portal, named below.

guides.title: Stamp duty in Chandigarh: 5% duty, fee capped at ₹10,000
guides.description: Chandigarh charges 5% stamp duty and a 1% registration fee capped at ₹10,000 on a sale deed, with the other deeds and the documents the sub-registrar asks for.
guides.answer: In the union territory of Chandigarh, the administration's rate sheet gives 5% stamp duty on a sale, gift or conveyance, "on value or amount of consideration (whichever is higher)", and a registration fee of 1% of the value, subject to a maximum of ₹10,000, plus a ₹20 pasting fee. The sheet is undated and shows no surcharge and no difference between men and women. The reference value, the "collector rate", is a separate schedule that Payotte did not read.

guides.title: Stamp duty concession for women buyers: states compared
guides.description: Which states give women a lower stamp duty rate on the official sheets Payotte read: Puducherry, Uttarakhand, Rajasthan. Rates, conditions, unconfirmed points.
guides.answer: There is no national stamp duty concession for women: it is a state or union territory matter. On the official sheets Payotte could read, three have a lower rate for a woman buyer: Puducherry (5% instead of 10%, for a woman permanently resident in the territory), Uttarakhand (3.75% instead of 5%, "upto 25 lakh") and Rajasthan (5% instead of 6%, or 4% for a woman in the SC, ST or BPL categories). Maharashtra's 1% reduction appears only in an editor's note and is not confirmed at the source. For other states, read the state's own sheet.

guides.title: Stamp duty and registration fee in Kerala: 8% and 2%
guides.description: Kerala charges 8% stamp duty and 2% registration on the higher of fair value and price. Sale, gift, partition and power of attorney rates from the sheet.
guides.answer: In Kerala a sale deed pays 8% stamp duty and a 2% registration fee, both on the fair value or the price in the deed, whichever is higher. That is the Registration Department's ready-reference sheet "as on 01.04.2023"; the 2019 version carried the same two rates, and no surcharge or cess appears in either. The sheet says it is "for informational purposes only", so check the current position at the sub-registrar's office before signing.

guides.title: Stamp duty in Maharashtra: Article 25 rates and Mumbai cess
guides.description: Stamp duty on a home sale in Maharashtra: 5% or 4% by area under Article 25, the Mumbai metro surcharge, the women's reduction and what is not confirmed.
guides.answer: In Maharashtra, stamp duty on the sale of a home is 5% of the market value inside a municipal corporation, a municipal council, a Nagar Panchayat or the Mumbai Metropolitan Region's rural areas, and 4% inside a gram panchayat area (Article 25(b), Maharashtra Stamp Act 1958, rates in force since 7 September 2017). Mumbai adds a 1% metro surcharge under section 144F of the Mumbai Municipal Corporation Act (the start date is set by notification, which Payotte did not read). Payotte could not read a registration fee schedule, so no registration fee figure is given here.

guides.title: Stamp duty and registration fee in Odisha: 5% and 2%
guides.description: Odisha charges 5% stamp duty and 2% registration on the sale of immovable property. The official fee table, other deeds, small fees and what is not read.
guides.answer: Odisha's Inspector General of Registration publishes a fee table on which "SALE IMMOVABLE" carries 5% stamp duty and a 2% registration fee. Both are percentages of the value; the table shows no minimum stamp amount for a sale and no ceiling on the fee. The page is undated, the base value is not named on it, and a concession for women buyers was not found, so none is applied.

guides.title: Stamp duty in Puducherry: 10%, or 5% for women residents
guides.description: Puducherry charges 10% stamp duty and 1.5% registration on the higher of price and guideline land rate; 5% for a woman buyer resident in the territory.
guides.answer: The Registration Department of the union territory of Puducherry lists a sale ("Conveyance (Sale)") at 10% stamp duty and 1.5% registration fee, both "on the sale value of the property or the G.L.R. value whichever is higher". A woman purchaser pays 5% stamp duty and the same 1.5% fee. The department's FAQ calls this a "50 % stamp duty concession" for women permanently residing in the territory, with a list of address proofs. The page is undated, so confirm the rates at the sub-registrar's office before signing.

guides.title: Stamp duty in Rajasthan: 6%, women's rate and the surcharge
guides.description: Rajasthan sale deed stamp duty of 6% on market value, 1% registration, the rebates on the official sheet and the surcharge question that is not settled.
guides.answer: On Rajasthan's official fee sheet "as applicable on 01-05-2024", a general sale deed pays 6% stamp duty on market value and a 1% registration fee, plus a ₹300 copying, scanning and indexing fee. The same sheet gives women 5% (or 4% for a woman in the SC, ST or BPL categories). The sheet also announces a surcharge on stamp duty ("10+20 = 30%"), but its application to a sale deed is not confirmed in the text Payotte could read, so it is not included in any figure below.

guides.title: Stamp duty in Uttarakhand: 5%, 3.75% for women, fee cap
guides.description: Uttarakhand stamp duty on a home sale is 5%, 3.75% for a woman buyer, with a 2% registration fee capped at ₹25,000. Rates, rebates and the ₹25 lakh point.
guides.answer: In Uttarakhand, the Stamp and Registration Department's sheet published in March 2025 puts stamp duty on a sale deed of immovable property at 5%, and 3.75% for a female buyer, "upto 25 lakh there after 5 %". The registration fee is 2% of the value, with a maximum of ₹25,000. The wording on the ₹25 lakh limit is ambiguous, so the reduced rate is shown here as applying at most up to ₹25 lakh.
